project: Hasamex European Robotic Surgery Market Study

guide_questions.question: How would you describe current adoption of robotic surgery in your market?

expected_expert_quotes.expected_substring: concentrated in larger academic hospitals and private centres with stronger capital budgets
Large university hospitals are much more advanced, while many smaller hospitals are still waiting
in some larger NHS trusts robotic surgery is becoming standard for selected procedures

guide_questions.question: What are the main barriers to adoption?

expected_expert_quotes.expected_substring: The biggest issue is still capital budget approval
Cost is the first barrier. These are large capital purchases
Funding is important, but I would say training capacity is just as important

guide_questions.question: How important are hospital budgets and ROI in purchasing decisions?

expected_expert_quotes.expected_substring: Very important. The clinical argument may get surgeons interested, but the finance team wants to understand utilisation
A strong clinical case helps, but the economic case decides whether it gets approved
I would say economics and clinical strategy are balanced

guide_questions.question: How important are surgeon training and clinical outcomes?

expected_expert_quotes.expected_substring: If only one surgeon can use the system, the economics become difficult
Very important operationally. If the hospital buys a system but only one surgeon is comfortable using it, utilisation will be poor
The key point is that adoption is not just about buying the machine

guide_questions.question: What adoption trend do you expect over the next 3–5 years?

expected_expert_quotes.expected_substring: I would expect maybe 15 to 20 percent more procedures annually in some of the stronger centres
closer to high single digits or low double digits in procedure volumes rather than something like 20 percent
I could see procedure growth above 15 percent annually in some areas

guide_questions.question: What is the typical hospital decision-making timeline for purchasing a new robotic system?

expected_expert_quotes.expected_substring: Six to twelve months is realistic once the hospital becomes serious
Nine to eighteen months is common. Procurement, clinical leadership, finance and management all need to align
Around six to nine months can happen if funding is already available
